To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the oxidation of ascorbate by molecular oxygen is accelerated by surfactants and that this effect is due to an increase in the rate constant for the rate-limiting step of the reaction, which is a one-electron transfer.

the rate of oxidation of ascorbate increases as the concentration of surfactant is increased up to a critical concentration, which is less than the critical micelle concentration of the surfactant, and then decreases as the concentration of the surfcatant is increased to the critical micelle conentration of the surfactan.

the rate of oxidation of ascorbic acid in the presence nonionic surfactant, poloxalkyl, increases as the concentration of surfactant increases up to the CMC and decreases at surfactant concentration above the CMC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of two non-ionic surfactants on the aerobic oxidation rate of ascorbic and the thermodynamic parameters of this reaction.
the effect of two non-ionic surfactants on the kinetics of ascorbic oxidation.
the effect of two non-ionic surfactants on the kinetics of ascorbic oxidation and the thermodynamic parameters for the oxidation of ascorbate in the presence of surfactant.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
nonionic surfactant micelles do not act as a catalytic site for the aerobic oxidation of AA.
surfactant molecules, at concentrations below their CMC, can act as catalysts for the autoxidation of ascorbic acids.
nonionic surfactant micelles are effective in increasing the rate of the oxidation of ascorbate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
surfactants, at low concentrations, enhance the rate of ascorbic oxidation.
the presence of surfactants in the solution increases the rate of ascorbic oxidation, but only at concentrations well below the CMC.
the presence of non-ionic surfactants increases the rate of oxidation of ascorbate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
surfactants have the potential to affect the kinetics of reactions in solution, even at concentrations well below the CMC.
the surfactant molecules are adsorbed on the surface of ascorbic molecules and this adsorption process increases the rate of the reaction.
nonionic surfactant can be used to control the rate of ascorbic oxidation.
